issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to a Meal class (and Main uses Meal), and the instructions state Meal is fully implemented. However, the template repository contains an Order.java class that duplicates the Meal semantics and an empty Meal.java file. This class-name/type mismatch and the missing Meal implementation in the template will confuse students about which type to use and prevents them from following the exercise (they may implement against Order or be blocked by the empty Meal).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the problem statement: provide a proper Meal.java implementation in the template (matching the Meal class in the solution) and remove or rename the extraneous Order.java. Update the template Main comments to reference Meal rather than Order so students have the expected starting types.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to a 'Meal' class as the core entity representing an orderable meal, but the template repository provides an 'Order' class with the same structure and purpose while the template's Meal.java is empty. This mismatch (Meal vs Order) creates an unnecessary mapping burden: students reading the problem expect to work with Meal, but starter code exposes Order, leading to confusion about which class to use or implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifiers so the same conceptual entity uses one name across artifacts. Rename the template's Order class to Meal (move/rename Order.java -> Meal.java and update references in template comments/Main), or add a Meal class in the template that delegates to or replaces Order. Ensure Meal.java is implemented in the template to match the problem description and solution.
